A minor annoyance I have endured with growing frequency is the presence of the unironed shirt. Not the sort that wrinkles when you fold it, or even the kind that requires steam—no, I’m speaking of the shirt that has been entirely neglected by the iron’s gentle touch and yet presented to the world as if it had just emerged from a dry cleaner’s chamber of wonders. It is the shirt that hangs off the shoulders like curtains in a draft, the collar that slumps forward in a manner that suggests defeat rather than fashion. It is, in short, the shirt that speaks of carelessness or, worse, indifference.
